text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- Transport Minister Rudolf Scholten has big hopes for solving Austria's transit problems. A treaty between the European Union and Switzerland could solve a lot of problems for Austria by means of greater rail capacity and raising the maximum weight of trucks in Switzerland.

- Bank Austria chief Gerhard Randa has said that a sale of the government's stake in Bank Austria could be done by the end of the year. However, Finance Minister Viktor Klima has denied any need for such a move.
- U.S. sport giant Scott wants to take over Austrian ski maker Blizzard for about 50 to 90 million schillings.

- Bank Austria has opened the Investmentbank Austria in London to drum up investors for Eastern Europe. Bank Austria is also interested in buying Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank. An offer is to be made soon, Creditanstalt has already presented a bid for that bank.
- Austria's budget deficit is slightly lower than expected at 5.9 percent of GDP, however this is still the highest level ever reached by Austria.

- Oberbank chief Hermann Bell, member of the consortium to take over Creditanstalt, has called the CA offer an Austrian solution. He also said there was always room for Die Erste savings bank, as long as they would not dominate CA.

- After having left the consortium, Die Erste savings bank hopes for a new call for bids for the government's stake in CA. Finance Minister Viktor Klima still has to check if the Italo-German-dominated consortium is still "Austrian" enough.
- The first half of 1996 was very bad for most of Austria's listed companies but prospects for the second half are better.
